title: Flight Changed? How to Update Your Airport Ride
description: A practical airport ride checklist for a canceled flight, missed connection, rebooking or diversion, including a message to send your transportation provider.
cta: Keep your airport ride aligned with your travel plans.
image_alt: Raindrops on an airport window with a softly blurred aircraft and warm lights across a blue-gray apron at dusk.
body:
If your flight changes after you have booked an airport ride, contact the transportation provider using the day-of-trip details on your confirmation. Explain what has changed, what is still uncertain and which reservation it affects. Obtain acknowledgment and an updated pickup plan before assuming the car booking follows the new itinerary.

A later arrival on the same flight, a replacement flight tomorrow and a landing at another airport need different conversations. Use the steps below to separate a status update from a request to change or cancel the ride.

Start with what is confirmed

Check the airline's app, website or staff for your current itinerary. A possible replacement flight is not the same as a confirmed booking, and a diversion airport is not automatically your final destination. Tell the ride provider promptly that a disruption has occurred, even if you cannot yet supply a new arrival time.

For a Bay Area arrival, the official SFO flight-status page, SJC flight-status page and flight search on OAK's airport website can help you cross-check the flight. SFO and SJC also direct travelers to confirm status with the airline. These pages report flight information; they do not confirm a change to your chauffeur reservation.

Identify which situation applies

  • Same flight, later arrival: send the updated estimate and ask whether the existing pickup arrangement still applies. Keep the flight number and local arrival date in the message.
  • Missed connection or replacement flight: send the final inbound flight into the pickup airport, not just the first leg of the trip. If no replacement is confirmed, say so and agree on when you will update the provider.
  • Cancellation with no new travel plan: ask what needs to happen to the existing ride reservation. Do not leave its status unresolved while you decide whether to travel.
  • New arrival airport: name the new airport explicitly and request a revised pickup arrangement. A car booked at SFO should not be assumed available at OAK or SJC.
  • Diversion: first confirm with the airline whether you will continue onward or leave at the diversion airport, and what happens to your bags. Do not send a chauffeur toward a temporary landing point based only on a flight-tracker alert.

Flight tracking can support arrival coordination, but do not assume it discovers a separate rebooking or authorizes a different route. Ask the provider to confirm what it is tracking and what you need to report yourself.

Check the date as carefully as the time

A late-night disruption can move the arrival to the next calendar day. Write the full local arrival date, the airport code and a clearly labeled time. Avoid messages such as 'now arriving at 12:30' without saying a.m. or p.m., the date or the time zone.

For example, if a traveler originally expected at SFO late Monday is rebooked into SJC early Tuesday, changing only the time leaves both the airport and date wrong. The revised request needs all three. This is a planning example, not a prediction of flight availability or ground journey time.

Resolve the original ride before relying on the replacement

Ask whether the provider can accommodate the new plan and whether it requires an amendment, a new reservation or cancellation of the original ride. Request the applicable revised quote and change, cancellation or waiting terms. Do not assume that an airline disruption makes ground-transport changes free or that the original rate applies to a different airport.

If you arrange alternative transportation, tell the original provider and obtain acknowledgment of the original reservation's status. Keep both references if a new reservation is issued. This helps avoid two active pickup plans or a chauffeur waiting for a flight you will no longer take.

A change message you can copy

Airport ride update
Ride reference: [reservation reference].
Original arrival: [airport, airline/flight, local date and time].
What changed: [delay, cancellation, rebooking, missed connection or diversion].
Confirmed new arrival: [airport, final inbound flight, local date and time], or [not yet confirmed].
Requested action: [review pickup change / confirm cancellation process / discuss options].
Passenger contact: [reachable number already agreed for the ride].
Other changes: [destination, passengers, luggage or boarding needs].
Please confirm receipt, availability, any revised price or terms, and what happens to the original reservation.

Send the relevant details rather than a full boarding pass or travel-document photo. If departure or pickup is close and you have no reply, use the provider's listed day-of-trip phone contact. An email or message marked sent is not acknowledgment that the ride has changed.

Close the loop with everyone traveling

Once the provider confirms the revision, check the airport, local date, flight, destination and passenger contact against the new itinerary. Get the pickup instructions for the new terminal or airport; do not reuse an old meeting point. If you booked for another person, send the revised confirmation to the traveler and retire the old instructions. The passenger handoff checklist covers that exchange.

After landing, communicate any further issue that affects when you are ready, such as waiting for bags or speaking with airline staff. Follow the agreed pickup and waiting arrangements rather than treating the flight's landing time as a guarantee that you can leave the terminal.

For an existing Koast ride, use the contact information on your reservation confirmation and include its reference. If you are planning a new journey, review Koast airport transfers and share the confirmed itinerary when requesting the ride.
